Biomolecular emulators · solution scattering · experimental design

Where does BioEmu-1 fail against solution scattering, and what should be measured next?

Raw ensemble predictions against 399 SAXS profiles, what reweighting says about each miss, and a two-arm measurement design.

Natalija Stepurko · October 2026 · natalija-stepurko.com

BioEmu-1 [1] emulates a protein's conformational ensemble from its sequence. I scored its raw ensembles, with no reweighting, against 439 small-angle X-ray scattering (SAXS) profiles from SASBDB [4], using the public ensembles and back-calculated curves of PeptoneBench [3]; 403 profiles pass data-quality checks and 399 of those have a BioEmu-1 ensemble. The ensemble fits 37% of them at reduced χ² ≤ 2 (95% interval 32%–41%; median χ² 3.3, 2.3 for folded and 8.9 for disordered proteins). Reweighting sorts the misses: 65 are modestly reweightable, 91 strongly reweightable and 97 are not fit along the path. One expectation came out reversed: for disordered proteins the ensemble radius of gyration is 1.21 times the measured value at the median (1.12–1.28), and the conformers themselves are 1.35 times too large, so the excess is in the sampled chains. Two validation experiments test the campaign logic: the raw error cannot be predicted from sequence-level features (R² = 0.05), and the selection rule, fed with such predictions, picks informative profiles no better than chance on held-out folds. The campaign therefore has a replication arm under one condition and a pre-specified test of the extension bias with matched controls chosen from the model alone.

All the code is public. Every number and figure on this page comes from the pipeline in this repository, which downloads the public inputs, scores them and writes the campaign proposal.Natalija-Stepurko/bioemu-saxs-campaign

Method

A biomolecular emulator predicts the set of shapes a protein adopts in solution, and how often, from its sequence alone. BioEmu-1 was trained on predicted structures, molecular-dynamics simulations and measured stabilities [1]; its successors will be trained with new experimental data, and choosing those experiments is the job this study rehearses. SAXS reports the overall size and shape distribution of a protein in solution, and 439 curated profiles with sequences are public [4, 3]. BioEmu conformers have served as a pool for SAXS ensemble selection on a few dozen proteins, where the unweighted pool did not reproduce the data [2], and PeptoneBench ranks generators by their fit after reweighting [3]; neither asked where the raw model fails by protein class, or what that implies for the next measurements.

  1. off-the-shelf
    439 measured SAXS profiles with sequence, pH and per-residue disorder score: PeptoneDB-SAXS, curated from SASBDB [4, 3].
  2. off-the-shelf
    100 BioEmu-1 conformers per protein, sampled by the PeptoneBench authors from the sequence alone.
  3. off-the-shelf
    One scattering curve per conformer, computed by the PeptoneBench authors with Pepsi-SAXS [6] on each profile's q grid.
  4. computed here
    Average the conformer curves with equal weights; fit one scale factor [5] and one constant background; report reduced χ² against the measured errors, and a second score that does not weight by them.
  5. computed here
    Guinier radius of gyration of the data and of the ensemble curve; flags for aggregation (low-angle upturn), over-subtraction (intensity below −3σ) and oligomers (SASBDB measured mass against sequence mass).
  6. computed here
    Maximum-entropy reweighting [7] along a path of decreasing prior strength; the effective sample fraction φ kept at χ² targets sorts each entry into one of four kinds.
  7. computed here
    The same scoring for 6 comparator models on the shared entries: four ensemble generators and two single-structure predictors as reference baselines.
  8. computed here
    Rank candidates for measurement; test whether the error can be predicted before measuring and whether the selection rule beats chance; write the two-arm campaign.

Where the raw ensemble fails

The raw ensemble fits 37% of profiles (95% interval 32%–41%; median χ² 3.3, quartiles 1.4–10.9). By class, 46% of folded, 24% of partly disordered and 12% of disordered profiles fit (E1 met).

A second score tells a different story about the classes. χ² weights every point by its reported error. A normalised root-mean-square deviation of ln I over the usable q range, which does not, gives 0.030 for folded, 0.034 for partly disordered and 0.031 for disordered proteins, with overlapping intervals: the class ordering of the χ² medians is partly a property of the reported errors. The ordering of the seven models is the same under both scores.

Error and chain length. E2 is not met: the rank correlation among folded proteins is weak (ρ = +0.09). What the data show is a step: folded proteins of up to 100 residues fit 67% of the time (n = 15), longer ones 45% (n = 231).

The size finding: disordered ensembles are too extended

E4 predicted over-compaction of disordered proteins, the usual failure of models trained on folded structures. The data show the reverse. The ensemble radius of gyration is 1.21 times the measured value at the median for disordered proteins (95% interval 1.12–1.28, two-sided Wilcoxon on the log ratio p < 0.001, n = 41), above 1 in 76% of them, against 0.98 for folded proteins (interval 0.98–0.99). Dropping the five most extreme ratios leaves a median of 1.19 (1.07–1.24, p < 0.001). The ratio grows with chain length within the class (Spearman ρ = +0.35, p = 0.03).

Is the extension in the conformers or in the forward model? For every clean disordered entry and 40 random folded ones I computed the radius of gyration from the Cα coordinates of the sampled conformers, and compared it with the measured Rg. For disordered proteins the coordinate Rg is 1.35 times the measured value (1.20–1.47), larger than the curve-derived 1.21: the sampled chains themselves are too large, and the forward model takes the ratio down, not up (curve over coordinates 0.92). For folded proteins the coordinates give 0.91 and the curves 0.95; the difference is the hydration layer that the forward model adds to a compact particle.

Among the 439 profiles there are no two identical sequences; 38 pairs are near-duplicates (5-mer Jaccard ≥ 0.5, about 93% identity or closer), and collapsing each cluster to one value leaves the disordered median at 1.21 (1.12–1.30) and the raw-fit share at 36%.

What reweighting says about each miss

The ensemble's conformer weights are moved towards the data by maximum-entropy reweighting [7], with decreasing strength of the prior, and χ² is tracked against the effective sample fraction φ that survives. Four kinds follow from the path: raw fit (raw χ² ≤ 2), modestly reweightable (χ² ≤ 2 reached while keeping φ ≥ 0.5), strongly reweightable (χ² ≤ 2 reached only with φ < 0.5) and not fit along the path. Of the 399 profiles, 146 are raw fits, 65 modestly reweightable, 91 strongly reweightable and 97 not fit.

kinddefinitionn (φ threshold 0.5)threshold 0.3threshold 0.7
raw fitraw χ² ≤ 2146146146
modestly reweightableχ² ≤ 2 reached while keeping φ ≥ 0.5659148
strongly reweightableχ² ≤ 2 reached only with φ < 0.59165108
not fit along the pathχ² ≤ 2 never reached979797

The threshold moves entries between the two reweightable kinds only; the raw-fit and not-fit counts do not depend on it.

Interpretation. A strongly reweightable entry is read as one where the right conformers are present and mis-weighted, so a profile of it carries a usable training signal; a not-fit entry needs a different measurement or a different model, because SAXS says the ensemble is wrong without saying how; a modestly reweightable entry needs a small, consistent correction, often of the Rg scale. Two cautions limit this reading: φ measures how concentrated the weights become, not information content; and SAXS is low-dimensional, so distinct ensembles can give the same curve.

Other models on the same profiles

The same archive carries back-calculated curves from other models for the same entries, scored here identically and without reweighting. The primary comparison is with the ensemble generators Boltz-2, IDPFold, idpSAM, PepTron; the single-structure predictors AlphaFold2 and ESMFold are reference baselines, since one structure cannot be reweighted and its best fit is its raw fit. Five further folders are not used: Boltz-1x and ESMFlow are superseded by models already included, idpGAN and IDP-o are disorder-only generators represented here by idpSAM, and PepTron-base is the un-finetuned PepTron. AF-CALVADOS [10] is a further ensemble method evaluated on this benchmark whose predictions were not in the archive.

Among the six comparators on the shared entries, BioEmu-1 has the lowest median raw χ² and the ranking is the same under the error-free score. PepTron comes closest: it beats BioEmu-1 on 40% of the 399 shared entries (95% interval 36%–45%), with a median log₁₀ χ² ratio of +0.02. On disordered proteins, BioEmu-1 is the only one of the seven whose median Rg ratio is above 1.1; PepTron 1.01, AlphaFold2 1.01, IDPFold 1.00, ESMFold 0.88, Boltz-2 0.52, idpSAM 0.40 on the same entries.

Can the error be predicted before measuring?

A campaign that chooses what to measure needs to know, before measuring, where the model is likely to be wrong. I fitted predictors of the raw error (log₁₀ χ²) and of the kind (strongly reweightable or not fit) from quantities known before a profile exists: chain length, disorder score and class, sequence composition (charge, hydrophobic, aromatic, proline and glycine fractions), the Rg expected from length by the scaling laws for folded and for disordered chains [9], and the model's own ensemble Rg and conformer spread. Nothing from the experimental curve enters. Evaluation is 5-fold cross-validation grouped by sequence cluster so that constructs of one protein never straddle a fold, repeated five times.

modelR² (log₁₀ χ²)MAEAUC (kind)Brier
constant / base rate-0.01 ± 0.010.4940.50 ± 0.000.252
class mean / class rate0.04 ± 0.010.4760.50 ± 0.020.251
ridge / logistic regression0.05 ± 0.010.4730.54 ± 0.030.255
gradient-boosted trees (depth 3)0.00 ± 0.010.4710.60 ± 0.020.254

Mean ± sd over the five repeats; n = 399 entries in 346 sequence groups; positive rate 47%.

The error is not predictable from these features at this sample size: the best regression reaches R² = 0.05 (class means alone give 0.04), and the best classifier an AUC of 0.60 with a Brier score no better than the base rate. The one feature the tree model leans on is the spread of the conformers' Rg (interquartile range over median) (importance 0.065 ± 0.047), and the calibration curve is close to the diagonal only because the predictions hardly leave the base rate.

Does the selection rule pick informative measurements?

The campaign ranks candidates by log₁₀ raw χ² × a kind weight × a tractability weight. To test the rule without circularity I treated the 399 profiles as a pool and asked, on held-out folds, whether the rule fed with predicted quantities (from the models above, fitted on the training folds) picks entries whose profiles would move the ensemble. Three policies: random; largest predicted raw error; the priority rule with predicted error and predicted kind weight. The same rule with the observed quantities is the ceiling. Objectives among the top k: the share of strongly reweightable or not-fit entries, and the mean φ-reduction (1 − φ at the χ² target, 1 when never reached).

policytop 10: share strongly reweightable or not fitφ-reduction at χ² = 1at χ² = 2top 20: shareφ-reduction at χ² = 1at χ² = 2
random0.48 ± 0.000.920.460.47 ± 0.000.910.46
predicted error0.58 ± 0.070.910.570.57 ± 0.020.900.54
predicted priority0.52 ± 0.030.890.510.53 ± 0.040.900.51
observed priority (ceiling)1.00 ± 0.010.980.800.93 ± 0.010.970.79

Mean ± sd over five repeats of the grouped 5-fold split; random is averaged over 200 draws per fold. The pool shares are 47% strongly reweightable or not fit and a φ-reduction of 0.91 at χ² = 1 (77% of entries never reach it, which is why that objective hardly moves).

With predicted quantities the rule is no better than chance: 0.52 of the top ten are strongly reweightable or not fit against 0.48 for random choice, a difference of +0.04 where a single random pick of ten spreads by ±0.15. Ranking by predicted error alone does slightly better (0.58, +0.10 ± 0.07 over repeats), still within that spread. With the observed quantities the rule picks 1.00, so the rule itself separates the kinds; what is missing is a predictor of them. This evaluation is retrospective: a profile that already exists carries no new information for the model, and the test says only how far the rule can be trusted to rank unmeasured proteins from what is known about them.

The measurement campaign

The proposal has two arms, each with constructs, assay, scripted quality criteria, success criteria, contingencies and work packages for an external provider.

Every candidate's measured molecular weight matches its sequence mass within the monomer range.

Re-measuring deposited systems under one buffer, one temperature, with tags removed and a concentration series controls the conditions the model does not see, and so removes the part of the raw error that is condition mismatch; it adds no new region of sequence space. A novel-acquisition sub-list, sequences without a SASBDB entry chosen by the error predictor, is not offered, because that predictor is not predictive (R² = 0.05); only the replication list stands. The kind and tractability weights of the ranking are heuristics set by judgement; the section above says how far they were validated: the rule separates the kinds when fed observed quantities and does not when fed predictions.

Arm 2 · hypothesis test: are BioEmu-1's disordered ensembles too extended?

The test arm takes disordered proteins whose BioEmu-1 ensemble Rg exceeds the scaling-law Rg for disordered chains (1.927 N0.598 Å [9]) by more than 10%, a quantity computed from the model alone, spanning chain length and net charge (19 of 41 disordered entries qualify); matched controls are disordered proteins of the same length bins whose ratio is within 10% of 1 (13 qualify). Pre-specified outcome: the median of Rgexp/Rgmodel across the test arm from Guinier fits of the new profiles. The bias is refuted if that median is at least 0.95; it is confirmed if it is at most 0.90 in the test arm and at least 0.95 in the controls. In the archive the test candidates have a median observed Rgmodel/Rgexp of 1.36 and the controls 1.19; the campaign repeats this under one condition with the selection made before any curve is seen.

The assay is size-exclusion-coupled SAXS at three concentrations with a protein standard in every session, tags removed, one standard buffer recorded with each dataset, and a repeat of one deposited entry per batch as a cross-site control. Six quality criteria (Guinier linearity, no low-angle upturn, no radiation damage across frames, molecular weight from I(0) within 20% of the sequence mass, no negative intensities, control reproduced at χ² < 2) decide pass or fail from recorded values. Not-fit cases get hydrogen–deuterium exchange mass spectrometry on the same batch of protein. Every batch of twelve constructs re-runs this pipeline on its new profiles, so the error map is updated before the next batch is chosen.

Limits

The ensembles are from the PeptoneBench archive, generated with BioEmu at code commit ac7455d; the archive does not record the checkpoint version, and re-sampling with the current v1.2 checkpoint is the first follow-up. SASBDB profiles differ in buffer, temperature and construct, none of which the model sees, so part of the raw error is condition mismatch, which a campaign under one standard condition removes. The forward model is treated as exact; its hydration-shell parameters bias Rg by a few per cent, which is why modestly reweightable cases are read with care, and the coordinate-derived Rg of the disordered conformers stands apart from it. Disorder classes come from a sequence-based predictor, not from the data. The model comparison is restricted to the six comparators on the shared entries. The validation experiments are retrospective and use 399 entries; a predictor that fails at this size could succeed with more data or with features from the model's own ensemble beyond its Rg and spread. Profiles with an upturn above 10%, an intensity more than three standard errors below zero, no valid Guinier region, or a measured mass above 1.6 times the sequence mass are kept out of every statistic (1, 12, 7 and 18 profiles; the oligomers' median raw χ² is 9.8).
